claim: Human developers spend most debugging time updating a mental model, not fixing: 57% model update vs 13% fix (Li and Coblenz, 12 people, 17 tasks); a failed first fix sent them back to model update in 9 of 17 tasks. Other field studies put comprehension at 35% (Ko), 58% (Xia 2018, 78 pros, 3148 h) to 70% (Minelli), so 57% is mid-range and depends on method.
agent_test: Log the share of tokens spent on read/trace/model-update vs patch in our agent; test a variant that caps patch tokens until a model note exists, at equal total tokens.

claim: Seeking and relating code is the main cost: in Ko 2006 35% of non-interrupted time went to navigation between fragments and about 36% to inspecting irrelevant code; 88% of searches in debugging tasks led to nothing later useful.
agent_test: Count wasted file opens and searches per task; test whether a running relevant-so-far list in S2 cuts wasted opens.

claim: Asking and answering why-did / why-did-not questions about runtime behaviour speeds diagnosis: Whyline cut time to diagnosis by 7.8x in six scenarios and gave 40% more tasks completed (N=9, tiny); in a later study median 4 vs 10 minutes. About half of novice errors came from false assumptions.
agent_test: Force the agent to write a why-not-X question and answer it with one run before patching; compare fix rate at equal tokens.

claim: Explicit hypotheses help when prompted: developers who reported a correct hypothesis at stage 2 had about 5x odds of fixing; supplying candidate hypotheses raised fix odds about 6x, but supplying fault locations did not (p=0.67). Without prompting, professionals voiced only casual thoughts and no formal hypotheses. For LLMs, AutoSD's explicit hypothesis loop matched but did not beat a plain LLM on repair rate; the value came from running experiments.
agent_test: Arm A: free debugging. Arm B: must keep a ranked hypothesis list with one discriminating test each. Equal tokens, SWE-bench Lite or debug-gym.

claim: Interactive debugger access helps strong models and hurts or does nothing for weak ones: debug-gym SWE-bench Lite, Claude 3.7 rewrite 37.2 vs debug 48.4 vs debug(5) 52.1; Llama-3.3-70B 2.4/4.0/4.8; Aider GPT-4o 69.7 vs 72.9, o3-mini 95.2 vs 94.2. Debug2Fix: forcing a debug call before editing lifted GPT-5 60.2 to 73.1 on GitBug-Java, while optional tools lowered scores (agent used the tool in 9% of cases). AutoSD adds: with real debugger output, runs yield a plausible patch 73% vs 63% when debugger output is imagined by the LLM.
agent_test: Compare optional vs forced probe-before-edit rule for our agent; report tool-call rate.

claim: Agent self-feedback is a weak substitute for a correct diagnosis: GPT-4 repair success was 33.30% with its own feedback vs 52.60% with human feedback (16 humans, 40 programs); on APPS 10 samples+1 repair each = 1.05x pass@20, so repair is barely better than resampling at equal compute. Intrinsic self-correction often does not help without an oracle signal.
agent_test: Equal-token test: N independent samples vs 1 sample + k repair rounds, with and without an executable test as feedback.

claim: Localization is not the main failure of current agents: right file found in 72-81% of failed runs; 60-69% of failures on several models edit the right functions yet give a wrong patch; 12 never-solved tasks failed from gaps in architectural reasoning, not patch difficulty.
agent_test: Score our S2 notes for causal explanation, not just location; check correlation with success.

claim: Run length is confounded with difficulty: failed runs are longer in Majgaonkar (SWE-agent +12.6%/+18.5%, OpenHands +31%/+82.5%), but within contested tasks in Mehtiyev (9,374 trajectories) resolved runs are longer (44.0 vs 39.6 steps; 263 of 416 tasks, p=1.9e-9). Sources disagree until difficulty is controlled.
agent_test: Do not use stop-when-steps-exceed-X as a rule; test step-budget stops against a difficulty-matched baseline.

claim: Agents can lose a correct fix: in 5 cases a gold-identical patch appeared mid-run and was later destroyed; an edit-commit checkpoint recovered all 5. A consensus variant added only +3.0 pp Pass@1 on GPT-5 (p=0.08, not significant).
agent_test: Add a rule: when tests pass, snapshot and require a stated reason to overwrite; count regressions.

claim: Repairing process anti-patterns raised resolution in problematic instances: +23.5 pp (DeepSeek-R1, 17 inst.), +13.0 (V3, 23), +6.9 (46); oscillation cut over 90%. Selected on stubborn instances, so likely inflated by regression to the mean.
agent_test: Run loop detection (RepeatedView-type) on our traces and test the intervention on a random, not selected, instance set.

claim: Giving the agent a structural map of the codebase improves localization: LocAgent file Acc@5 on Loc-Bench 83.39 vs Agentless 67.50; SWE-bench Lite Acc@5 73.36 vs 58.39; Pass@10 37.59 vs 33.58. Hypothesis-and-investigation agents raised MAP 23-39% over baselines in bug-report localization (ablation: up to 19% from hypotheses). Gains in final repair are small (Pass@1 27.92 vs 26.31).
agent_test: Give a graph/skeleton map in S2 vs raw file reads; measure localization accuracy and fix rate at equal tokens.

claim: Interface choices shape the model: SWE-agent ablations (GPT-4 Turbo, Lite) summarized search 18.0 vs iterative 12.0; 100-line viewer 18.0 vs full file 12.7; edit with linting 18.0 vs without 15.0; last-5 observations 18.0 vs full history 15.0. Agentless skeleton view 58.33% vs full file 53.67% on element recall.
agent_test: Test compact observation history vs full history for S2 at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs are weak at tracing runtime behaviour without running code: 44.4% average on runtime behaviour reasoning (REval), CRUXEval GPT-4 63-67% (75-81% with CoT), CodeSense Python no model above 50%; tool use fixed 58% of the computation-error category. A mental model built only by reading is unreliable.
schema_part: S2 (verify by execution), G (evidence over belief)
agent_test: Compare predict-output-then-run vs just-run and log how often predictions are wrong.

claim: Dynamic knowledge is the hard part of a program model: in Burkhardt et al. (30 experts, 21 novices) situation model scored 4.36 vs program model 3.55 of 6; experts beat novices on situation model (4.56 vs 4.10) and static information (5.00 vs 4.36) but not on dynamic information.
agent_test: Tag S2 entries as static or dynamic and count how many dynamic facts come from execution.

claim: Familiarity changes tracing strategy: in Li and Coblenz, backward tracing was a dominant strategy at coarse levels (version history, files, calls), with git bisect used by P1 (under 5% familiar); more familiar developers leaned on forward tracing. Only 8 developers; descriptive, no test.
agent_test: Let the agent pick forward vs backward by a stated familiarity score; compare to a fixed mode.

claim: Benchmark validity limits all agent numbers: SWE-bench+ found 32.67% of successes had solution leakage and 31.08% passed on weak tests; filtered resolution fell from 12.47% to 3.97%; 94% of issues predate model cutoffs. Gap search adds: SWE-bench-Live best 19.25% vs 43.20% for the same pair on Verified; SWE-Bench Pro public best 43.6%, commercial best 17.8%; PatchDiff: 7.8% of patches pass without being correct, 6.4 pp inflation; models name the buggy file from issue text alone up to 76% on Verified vs up to 53% elsewhere.
agent_test: Report on a contamination-filtered or post-cutoff set.

claim: Long context hurts: Claude 3.5 Sonnet on LongSWE-Bench falls from 29% to 3% going 32K to 256K; Claude 2 declines as context grows in SWE-bench. A compact running S2 note may beat dumping files.
agent_test: Compare a compact S2 note vs full-file context at equal tokens.

claim: An explicit hypothesis-experiment loop for an LLM keeps repair rate level with a plain LLM but gives a usable confidence signal: bugs with a DONE conclusion were 89% correct vs 82% without. Imagined execution output removes the benefit (runs plausible 63% vs 73% with real execution). Developers (N=20) judged patches more accurately with the explanations in 5 of 6 real bugs.
schema_part: S2/S6 (hypotheses must be tested by running)
agent_test: A/B: hypothesis list with required executed check vs hypothesis list without execution, at equal tokens, on post-cutoff tasks.

claim: Fresh or private code is much harder than the standard benchmark: same agent-model pair 19.25% (SWE-bench-Live) vs 43.20% (Verified, same setup); SWE-Bench Pro public best 43.6%, private commercial best 17.8%. Context overflow (35.6%) and endless file reading (17.0%) are leading failure modes of Sonnet 4 on Pro.
agent_test: Measure our agent on SWE-bench-Live or Pro public tasks; log overflow and repeated-read counts with and without an S2 note.

claim: A fixed order of localization, then repair, then test selection (Agentless) matched the best open agents at low cost (32.00%, 0.70 USD, SWE-bench Lite, 2024), so a build-model-first step does not need the agent to decide when to stop. LLM-written reproduction tests are weak judges: 94 of 213 also passed on the true patch.
agent_test: Compare a fixed model-building budget against an agent-chosen stop at equal tokens.

claim: Gaps 1, 4, 6, 8 and 9 have no direct study found: no controlled test of a written running system model at equal tokens, no split of static vs dynamic vs causal model parts in agents, no validated stop signal, no study of model revision after a failed fix beyond oscillation counts. Search was limited by exhausted quota.
agent_test: Run these as our own experiments.
